newsitem.title: USA: Heart drug cuts hospital stay, does not extend life.
newsitem.headline: Heart drug cuts hospital stay, does not extend life.

text.p: The heart drug digoxin, also known as digitalis, does not help people with heart failure live longer but it does reduce the risk of hospitalization, a new study has concluded.

According to a report in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine, the death rate was 35 percent regardless of whether the 8,600 volunteers involved in the new research received digoxin or a placebo for three years.

However, "there were 6 percent fewer hospitalizations overall (in the digoxin group) than in the placebo group, and fewer patients were hospitalized for worsening heart failure," the researchers concluded.
The test was an attempt to resolve a controversy over digoxin, which is credited with relieving symptoms of heart failure, yet criticised for possibly having dangerous side effects.
"Both advocates and opponents of digitalis are likely to find solace in the results," said Dr. Milton Pack of Columbia University in an editorial in the Journal.
The drug is made by several manufacturers.
